description: Train, inspect, edit, automate, and export 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes from a single native application.
vibe: Discover before you code, mutate with intent, and never sleep on a job.
highlights: MCP-first workflow: prefer runtime discovery over reading C++ source
Strict separation of concerns: resources for state, tools for mutations
Explicit anti-guessing rule for operator ids, menu paths, panel ids, and UI tool ids
Long-running operations must be paired with job/event tools instead of sleeping
Post-mutation verification required (e.g., confirm selection writes with selection_get)
assessment: This guide demonstrates mature systems thinking by treating the MCP surface as the primary interface and enforcing a read-before-write discipline. The explicit prohibition on guessing identifiers and the requirement to verify mutations prevent the most common agent failure modes in complex GUI-driven applications. The playbook structure and job ID catalog give agents concrete, reproducible workflows rather than vague instructions.
